matchquality-scale-bias.note: matchQuality REWARDS UNDERSIZED outlines: sweeping a scale multiplier over shipped placements, q peaks at 0.85 on shiny/s-0bfc44d8 (visibly undersized) and only 1.00 on cream-caplets (visually correct). Consequence: the metric must NOT drive major/minor refinement until this is fixed — optimising size against it would visibly worsen the owner's standing complaint. Fix direction: scale the edge offset to pill size and/or require the step at the TRUE silhouette (largest gradient along the radial ray), not any step.

synthetic-corpus-must-be-single-medicati.note: tools/gen-pills.html drew a NEW RANDOM COLOUR PER PILL until 2026-08-12 (drawRound: `light = PILL==='white' || rand()<0.6` then a 3-colour pick; drawCapsule: `CAP_COLORS[(rand()*4)|0]`), both INSIDE the draw loop. That produced green+white and white/pink/orange pills in a single frame — a direct violation of the owner's scope rule that a photo shows ONE medication (same size AND shape AND colour scheme; a consistent two-tone split is fine, per-pill random colours are OUT of scope). 186 of the corpus's synthetics were affected; 174 of them PASSED anyway, purely on a lucky palette draw, while the 12 that failed did so for a scope reason, not an algorithm reason — the counter was correctly refusing to unify several different-coloured pill populations. Fixed by hoisting both colour draws OUT of the loop (ROUND_BASE / CAP_PAIR, chosen once per image from the seed) and regenerating all 186 with exact generator-emitted truth. DO NOT move a colour draw back inside a draw loop: it silently makes the corpus test something the product does not claim to do, and it hides real regressions behind luck.

glare-pulls-centres-toward-highlight.note: MEASURED 2026-08-12 on s-0bfc44d8. Placement centres on glossy pills are systematically displaced TOWARD THE SPECULAR HIGHLIGHT: mean displacement (-0.50, -7.91) px — horizontal component ~0, vertical -7.9px, i.e. 28% of the pill WIDTH (median offset 8.8px). The bias tracks gloss, not code: s-0bfc44d8 -7.91, s-eb90778f -3.37 (both shiny, both UP toward the light), vs r-7ff7fd99 -0.26 and r-295482c1 +1.17 (matte, no bias, opposite signs). A coordinate/scale bug would bias every image alike; this does not. MECHANISM: the shadowed LOWER rim falls below the foreground threshold and is lost. Mask coverage above vs below the pill centre is 35.5%/27.8% on shiny but 41.1%/42.3% on matte, and stages/mask-final.png shows blobs bitten off at the bottom, several shedding a detached crumb where the dark rim breaks up. IMPORTANT SCOPE: the mask truncation accounts for only ~3px of the ~7.9px (mask centroid dy = -2.98). The remaining ~5px comes from the stamp fitting the truncated blob. Fixing the mask is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT — do not expect the offset to vanish by widening the threshold, and re-measure both numbers after any change.

regress-baseline-is-untracked-and-self-o.note: tools/regress.mjs WRITES tools/baselines/counts.json on every run, and that file is UNTRACKED — so a run of a bad build silently installs the bad numbers as the baseline, and the next comparison blesses a regression. Hit for real 2026-08-12: a rim-recovery experiment measured 218/251 and then 215/251 against a shipping 237/251, and left the baseline reading 215. Before trusting any comparison, check tools/baselines/counts.json's summary against the last KNOWN-GOOD gate number recorded in a commit message. SECOND TRAP, same day, cost six runs: piping regress.mjs through `tail` loses all output (it buffers to completion, and the wrapper reports an empty file that looks exactly like a silent crash). Pipe through `tee <file>` instead — the gate was never broken, the invocation was.

counts-can-be-right-for-wrong-reasons.note: MEASURED 2026-08-12 by tools/geomgate.mjs across the corpus: 407 overlapping placement pairs, 142 duplicates, 160 off-pill, in 65 of 219 images — MANY OF WHICH COUNT PERFECTLY. Cornerstone example synth2-rc-noise-small-n12-t65-s199.png: count 12/12 EXACT, but per-pill 8/12 with 4 MISSED and 4 SPURIOUS. The overlay shows a heap of stacked orange rings on a few beads while four real pills sit ringed red beside them. The errors cancel, so every count-based gate reports success. This is the 'lucky, not detecting' mode the stamp strategy exists to kill, and it is invisible to regress.mjs by construction. Run BOTH tools/geomgate.mjs --check AND tools/perpill.mjs --check before believing a counter change is good; a count-only green is not evidence. The failures cluster hard in dense touching sets (-small- with t65 = 65% touching), which is where placements have the least room and the partition is least constrained. QUANTIFIED 2026-08-12 across the full corpus: of the 20 images with geometry violations, SIXTEEN COUNT EXACTLY. The dominant signature is equal-and-opposite error — synth2-rc-dark-small-n60-t65-s111 is 60/60 EXACT with per-pill 53/60 (7 missed, 7 spurious, 57 overlaps, 25 duplicates), and s199 is 12/12 EXACT with 8/12 (4 missed, 4 spurious). Phantoms cancel misses inside dense touching clusters, so the count is a coincidence. The pose refiner fix moved the corpus 407 -> 389 overlapping pairs (4%), which is real but marginal: it can only re-pose pills, and the defect is that the wrong NUMBER of pills is created inside one blob upstream.

adversarial-suite-exposes-hex-raft-colla.note: tools/gen-adversarial.{html,mjs} builds 36 deliberately hostile layouts with EXACT generator truth (hexraft/chain/ring/pair/cross/lonely/dense/bimodal). First run 2026-08-12: 10/36 exact overall, and on the FAIR subset (flat light/dark backgrounds, uniform pills, no noise) 6/19 exact with per-pill 78/384. The corpus completely hid this — it is mostly random scatter, so hard packings only ever arrived by accident. Headline failure: a HEX-PACKED RAFT of 19 obvious pills on a flat background returns count=1. The distance transform shows a SINGLE bright mound with faint spokes; touching pills leave no background between them, the DT never dips, and watershed yields one basin. Fails identically at touch=0.96 (overlapping) and touch=1.04 (2% apart), so it is not a knife edge. chain and lonely score 100% — the defect is specifically 2-D packing, not contact per se. CAVEAT on the noise cases: the generator's confetti background is far harsher than any real photo and produced count=466 on a 7-pill image; treat noise-background results as generator artefacts until the background is made realistic, and judge progress on the light/dark/wood subset.

scale-estimate-is-the-keystone-on-hard-p.note: MEASURED 2026-08-12 by tools/raft-bakeoff.mjs on the adversarial suite. The raft failure was NOT primarily a segmentation problem — it was a SCALE problem. The pill radius is read from the DT ridge, which is only as good as the mask, and on a LIGHT board a pale pill barely clears the threshold: measured R=6.7 against a true 13 (half scale) while identical pills on a dark board measured 10.5. Every downstream technique then searches at the wrong scale and over-proposes 3-5x. Estimating scale from the PHOTO's autocorrelation (first peak = centre-to-centre pitch = 2R, which never consults a threshold) fixed R to 13.0 and improved EVERY technique at once: dt recall 45.5% -> 81.3%, hough 16 -> 21 exact, consensus spurious 248 -> 60. Every case where R comes out correct is now EXACT, including hexraft 37/37 and dense 120/120. All 6 remaining failures have R ~6-7 — the autocorrelation is silent when pills do NOT repeat (lonely/pair/chain on a light board), and an area-based fallback for those measured worse (21 -> 19 exact) because a merged raft's area implies a huge radius. Scale on a low-contrast background with non-touching pills is the open problem.

geom-baseline-self-overwrites.note: Running `node tools/geomgate.mjs <one-image>` REWRITES tools/baselines/geom.json with that single image's numbers, silently replacing the corpus-wide baseline. It happened during the cluster-solver work: a one-image check left images:1 in the file and the next comparison read it as if it covered 219, which made a solver improvement look like a regression. Same class as the regress.mjs counts.json trap. For attribution, do a head-to-head instead: VALEYE_NO_CLUSTER=1 node tools/geomgate.mjs vs the plain run, same build. Measured that way the solver is 197->80 overlapping pairs, 59->16 duplicates, 85.1->39.8px worst penetration.

compare-only-against-a-fresh-run.note: A stored gate output is a snapshot of the build that produced it, and comparing a new run against a stale one manufactures phantom regressions. Hit TWICE: (1) tools/baselines/geom.json overwritten by a single-image run; (2) /tmp/geom-full.txt from Aug 13 compared against an Aug 17 run, which read as "physics made it 80 -> 145 overlapping pairs" until s111 was checked out at the pre-physics commit and measured IDENTICAL (17 pairs, 7 duplicates). Both physics changes were exonerated. Rule: for attribution, run BOTH arms on the SAME build in the same session (VALEYE_NO_CLUSTER=1 vs plain), and never trust a baseline file whose mtime you have not read.

cluster-solver-measured-three-ways.note: Cluster solver attribution, all three arms run on ONE build (183f7b3): solver OFF = 197 overlapping pairs / 59 duplicates / 85.1px worst over 59 of 219 images; solver ON with deletion BLOCKED = 145 / 44 / 43.1px over 48; solver ON with deletion ALLOWED = 80 / 16 / 39.8px over 45. So the solver is -59% pairs and -73% duplicates, and blocking deletion was silently costing 65 pairs and 28 duplicates. off-pill rises 6 -> 19: separating two stacked placements leaves one off its material, which is a visibly wrong outline traded for an invisible miscount. If a future change makes the solver look weaker, check whether something is rejecting its deletions before concluding the solver regressed.

log-blob-is-not-a-detector.note: TRIED AND REJECTED: Laplacian-of-Gaussian at the known pill radius as a detector. In the region bake-off it posts the highest recall of any technique (97-100% on shiny/lined/real, and it is the ONLY technique that finds anything on lined paper where otsu and dt-peaks both score 0%), which makes it look like the answer. It is not: the ranking is worthless. On shiny/s-eb90778f the worst true pill ranks #4412 of 115328 peaks, so keeping the top 34 peaks recovers 3 of 34 pills. A shape score (disc uniformity x annulus contrast) was tried as a re-ranker and measured WORSE still: 0/34 in the top 34. The high recall is an artefact of generating ~115k candidates for 34 pills -- at that density almost anything is "found". Do not revisit without a fundamentally different candidate reduction.

lone-witness-cannot-win-the-panel.note: RECURRING DEAD END, reached three times from different directions. On lined-bfdbfef9 blob 1 the votes are ws:19 mass:14 crease:10 ero:3; truth is ~14, so mass alone is right, and the panel discards it because ks.length>=2 requires two agreeing methods. The same shape appears on adv-dense-light (ws:126, truth 120, base 139 wins). It is tempting every time. MEASURED ANSWER (tools/panel-audit.mjs, 128 disagreeing blobs): base is closest on 72 blobs, mass on 13, ws on 5. On the wide-divergence slice (base vs mass differ >=1.5x, 20 blobs) base still wins 12 to 8. Letting a lone witness win loses far more than it gains. Note also that k >= regs.length and corroboratedDescent contradict each other -- the floor always wins -- but that is NOT the operative blocker: measured over six failing images, descent-blocked fired 0 times because ks.length>=2 fails first.

bright-percentile-cue-costs-ten-images.note: TRIED TWICE AND REVERTED: adding a bright-percentile map as a third entrant to the cue retry, for pale pills on textured wood. The DIAGNOSIS is solid -- on wood the histogram is trimodal (pills ~250, pale grain ~180-200, dark grain ~120) so Otsu splits pale grain from dark grain and the mask comes out as horizontal GRAIN BANDS; cutting at the 99th luminance percentile recovers the pills exactly (measured coverage 9/9, 19/19, 8/8, 8/8, with the threshold jumping 129 -> 245 and nothing between). ATTEMPT 1, binary mask: worse -- distBg is a distance-like map and Otsu/DT/watershed all read gradient, so a hard 0/255 broke them (hexraft-wood 19 -> 15, stack 7 -> 5). ATTEMPT 2, graded distance-above-board: fixes hexraft-wood to 19/19 EXACT but costs the CORPUS ten images (239 -> 229). The coherence score lets it win on photos where the default map was fine. Any future attempt must gate on something that identifies a textured board specifically, not on the coherence score alone -- and must be measured against the full corpus, since the adversarial wood cases all improve while real photos collapse.

dense-board-count-vs-picture.note: The 120-pill dense board counts 142 while finding ALL 120 pills (0 missed, 22 spurious). Three measured attempts, all reverted: (1) IoU cut -- phantom median IoU 0.509 is IDENTICAL to real, because a phantom between two real pills still covers pill material. No threshold separates them. (2) Non-overlap cut -- phantom median penetration 14.35px vs real 3.71px, a 4x signal, but real pills reach 24.68px so no single cut works (pen>4px drops all 22 phantoms AND 50 real). (3) Prefer ws on photo-seeded blobs -- the evidence is strong (ws closer on 6 of 6, total error 22 vs base 70) and counts improve corpus-wide (dense 142->129, adversarial 35->36 exact, spurious 170->130), BUT the picture collapses: lowering k does not re-place the region, so dense went from 120/120 pills found to 7/120 and adversarial per-pill fell 719->577. CONCLUSION: the count and the placements are computed in different places, and moving one without the other trades a real picture for a better number. The panel runs at line ~4949 and the Lloyd placement at ~7069, so k CAN reach it -- the fix is to re-place the region at the panel k, not to decrement the count.

dense-board-overlap-peel.note: ATTEMPT 4 on the dense board (142 for 120, all 120 pills found). A GREEDY OVERLAP PEEL -- drop the single deepest-penetrating placement, re-measure, repeat -- works beautifully in isolation: at a 10px floor it gives 124 for 120 with all 120 pills still found and 6 spurious, so the count error falls from +22 to +4 with ZERO real pills lost. A plain threshold cannot do this (real pills reach 24.68px penetration), only the greedy re-measurement can. It still cannot ship. Unscoped it costs 20 corpus images (239 -> 219). Scoped by "packed fraction" (share of placements deep inside a neighbour: dense board 0.27, shiny 0.06, real photos 0.00) at a 0.15 cut it costs 2 -- synth2-rw-kraft-small-n30-t35-s291 (30 -> 25) and synth2-rc-dark-small-n60-t65-s111 (60 -> 53), both DENSE SYNTHETICS whose pills are legitimately packed. The packed-fraction signature cannot distinguish a genuinely dense board from one whose partition invented extra hypotheses, because they look identical by that measure. THREE IMPLEMENTATION TRAPS worth keeping: the peel must run BEFORE `const out = {count,...}` (line ~8109) or the decrement is captured too late and does nothing; single-pill regions carry no g.pills so collecting only g.pills sees 2 of 129 nodes; and a multi-pill region may lose EVERY placement, so a "never empty a region" guard silently discarded 15 of 16 peeled nodes.

browser-and-node-count-differently.note: The lab/test pages count live in the BROWSER; every gate (bake-parallel, adv-run, geomgate) runs in NODE with jpeg-js. The two JPEG decoders produce slightly different pixels and borderline images flip: measured 2026-08-19, t2-ibuprofen counts 13 EXACT in Node and 14 in the browser; t2-white-capsules-wood counts 8 EXACT in Node and 9 in the browser. Earlier the same divergence shifted blob IDs and areas on r-f5d11815 (blob 2/5706px browser vs blob 1/5751px Node). THE BROWSER IS THE SHIPPING ENVIRONMENT, so a Node-only gate certifies the wrong build. The owner sees "wrong" counts on the lab page that every local gate says are fixed. Path to closing it: test.html already re-runs the corpus in-browser (the "re-run live in browser" link); wire that into a headless-Chrome gate and report BOTH numbers, or make the pipeline robust to one-pixel mask jitter so the decoders agree. Also the geometry overlaps the owner keeps seeing are real even when counts are exact: physics on capsules-wood still ends at worstAfter 12.3px penetration.

chroma-mask-surgery.what: Saturation-Otsu mask union/carve at mask-final on lined-paper images

measured.union: no-op: by mask-final, rescue has already filled the mask FATTER than the chroma evidence (mask 15.2% of frame vs sat 11.2% on lined-69204ff4); sat components touching the mask added only 23-111 px
measured.carve: harmful: trimming mask >3px outside the saturated region removes shaded pill flanks along with junk -- counts fell 22->17, 19->18, 18->13 against truth 20/20/20

chroma-mask-surgery.lesson: Chroma on beige-pill/white-paper scenes reads the LIT face of the pill only; the shadow flank is neutral. Any mask surgery keyed on saturation amputates it. Chroma remains useful only as a late arbiter (existing chromagate), not as mask evidence.

splotchkill-color-exemption.what: Exempt splotchkill victims whose chromaticity matches the (non-neutral) pill population median, to save glare-shredded fragments
splotchkill-color-exemption.measured: On shiny/s-eb90778f the board is saturated brown leather and its glare streaks are red-brown: the exemption spared 7 of 9 kills (junk included), the surviving ragged fragments fractured placement, and the count moved 31->30 of 34 (wrong direction).
splotchkill-color-exemption.lesson: Population-color matching needs a hue GAP between board and medication. Works for lenjunk only because that gate additionally requires a NEUTRAL board (bgSatC<20). Any color-based rescue must first verify the board/pill chroma separation on the image itself.

shadow-in-mask-root-cause.what: Deep cast shadow enters the mask and corrupts EVERY downstream calibration at once

measured.unit: s229/shadowpair: pair- and shadow-bloated blobs push unit to ~2x a true single; raft-unit catches >2x but a pair sits at exactly ~2.0 and slips under
measured.unitLen: s229: isolated pill + shadow lobe reads major 61-64 vs true diameter 27, so unitLen=44.7 and every length-based gate (incl. roundness unitLen < 2.7r) is blind
measured.unitfix: derives from the same corrupted blob population; after raft-unit corrects the unit, unitfix reverts it (fixed for round pops via the circular-evidence veto, commit 32b2d440)
measured.template: a shadow-bridged pair is a smooth convex peanut and poisons tplPool too
measured.mask-shatter: shadowchain at depth 0.65 fragments pills into 134px crescents; medSingle collapses and one region mints units=23
measured.unitfix-veto-dead: confirmed by the committed-state adversarial baseline (39/56): the round scope (unitLen < 2.7r) closes exactly on pair-dominated boards because unitLen reads pair length -- shadowpair back to 0/2. The veto protects the corpus but cannot fire where needed. Same lesson: no length gate works until the mask stops swallowing shadow.

shadow-in-mask-root-cause.countermeasures_shipped: shadow-lobe descent (census+seam), p75 lenjunk, round-scoped unitfix veto, two-tone dark-mass witness
shadow-in-mask-root-cause.next: Mask-level shadow segmentation: per-blob, cut peripheral components with lum < ~0.5 x blob p75; gate on cut size and verify against shiny (dark pills) + lined (shaded flanks) before trusting. The round-raft-unit 1.55x rescue is written but DEAD because its unitLen gate is itself shadow-corrupted -- do not re-add without an uncorrupted length witness.

attempt-2026-08-20-shadowcut.design: At mask-final, per blob >=200px: p75 lum reference; candidates lum < 0.45 x p75; components >= 3% of blob cut; refuse if total > 60% of blob; hue guard (cut only components whose chroma differs >= 20 from the 0.55-0.95 x p75 BODY band -- the top of the histogram is glare on specular beads). Plus a splotchkill pill-scale refusal arm: >= 3 doomed with median area >= 0.5 x medGood = the population itself, refuse the stage.

attempt-2026-08-20-shadowcut.next-iteration: tighten the cut: require components to touch the blob rim AND border background (a cast shadow lies between pill and board); try min component 8% and cap 40%; diagnose t3 (+4 suggests the cut SPLIT blobs into extra pieces) before re-attempting.
attempt-2026-08-20-shadowcut.t3-diagnosis: DIAGNOSED: t3 is white tablets heaped on a BRIGHT YELLOW board. Inter-pill shadow seams are dark (<0.45 p75) and board-hued (dC>=20 from the white body), so both gates passed and the cut deleted the seams BETWEEN touching pills -- splitting fused blobs and double-counting contacts (+4). Refinement confirmed: a candidate component may only be cut if a majority of its boundary touches BACKGROUND (peripheral lobe), never when it borders pill material on both sides (seam). Seams must stay in the mask; the watershed owns them.

0bfc-half-bead-calibration.what: s-0bfc44d8 (-2): glare splits every bead lengthwise; region medSingle calibrates to a HALF-bead (whole beads read 2.0-2.07x medSingle at units=1), so the region-level unit is half the truth
0bfc-half-bead-calibration.measured: splotchkill wholesale-refused (14/37 doomed, population inversion). Misses at blobs 1/9/13 (areas 0.65-1.02 x blob-unit); spurious from blob 56 (massR 1.52) raised to units=2 by arc. The blob-level unit (~2600) is right; the REGION-level medSingle (~1283) is the half.
0bfc-half-bead-calibration.next: Reconcile region medSingle against blob-level unit: when regions systematically read ~0.5 x the blob unit on a population whose blobs are single (massR ~1), the watershed is splitting on glare seams -- merge half-regions along the glare axis before counting. Same lengthwise-glare signature the advil photos carry.

r-7ff7fd99-shingled-pair.what: r-7ff7fd99 (-1): blob 11 holds 4 truth pills but the watershed yields 3 pill-SIZED regions, and mass reads 3.16 because shingled caplets hide area under each other. The clear test accepts (mass ~= wsCount ~= unitsSum, every piece 1.0-1.19x unit) so the blob never reaches the panel.
r-7ff7fd99-shingled-pair.measured: truth (222.5,302.5) and (205.5,295.5) both map to one region at (211,298); region areas 601-727 against unit 657 -- all sane. A piece-size sanity gate was written and REVERTED as dead code: the fused pair looks exactly like one healthy pill.

count-right-picture-wrong.fix: One bounded translation per stamp toward the centre of mass of the connected component beneath it, capped at a quarter half-width per pass and iterated 4x, admitted only on a STRICT reduction in claimed background and no increase in penetration. salmon medOff 0.180 -> 0.155, maxOff 0.249 -> 0.180 (under the 0.25 flag bar); controls unchanged at 0.022 and 0.028. Gates all held: browser 258/262, Node 256/262, adversarial 51/56, per-pill 799/1020.
count-right-picture-wrong.refuted: SIX approaches, all by measurement. (1) centring tiebreak in fitScore: no effect -- clumpfit never sees a stamp single. (2) same tiebreak in poseScore: no effect, same reason. (3) routing singles through Lloyd ('units >= 1'): made centring WORSE everywhere, healthy r-f091e9e9 0.022 -> 0.119 and r-fd69dff9 0.028 -> 0.144, while salmon did not improve at all. (4) requiring the incumbent be fully on foreground (bg == 0): rejects exactly the markers that need help, since an off-centre stamp necessarily overhangs (the four read bg=3,3,3,4 of 25). (5) aiming at the sample grid's own foreground centroid: dragged by that same overhang, so the step is too small to pass its own improvement test. (6) allowing equal-background steps (nb > bg): better median but one marker OVERSHOT, salmon worst 0.180 -> 0.275, past the bar.
count-right-picture-wrong.gate: tools/centroidgate.mjs -- marker offset from its pill's centre of mass, in half-widths, on the counter's own single-certified regions. TRAPS: (a) grayToStage encodes foreground in the GREEN channel (0.86*255); testing red reports zero blobs and a silent all-clear. (b) mask-used and mask-final are NOT interchangeable -- see the retraction above. (c) anchor the reference pill area on single-certified regions, NOT a raw blob median: salmon's mask holds 23 components of which 17 are few-pixel specks, so the median reads 8px and a 1.6x filter rejects every real pill (the gate reported 'no isolated singles' on the one board it was built for). (d) g.shape is undefined on these regions -- the pose lives on pills[0].
count-right-picture-wrong.rule: Treat marker-to-centre-of-mass offset as a first-class metric alongside count. A change that improves the count while pushing markers off their pills is not an improvement.

raft-marker-placement-open.status: ALL THREE fix candidates refuted by measurement; mechanism understood, no safe lever found
raft-marker-placement-open.what: The operator's report covered two kinds of misplaced marker. The stamp-placed SINGLE is fixed (see count-right-picture-wrong). The second kind now has a measured root cause: on a LIGHT background the mask absorbs each pill's cast shadow, the blob's centre of mass moves into the shadow, and every marker follows it.
raft-marker-placement-open.evidence: Controlled by background on the same synthetic arrangement (adv-shadowlone-n8, identical pills and shadows, count EXACT on all three): light blob area 1214px vs pill 314px = 3.86x, marker bias 0.676 half-widths at 52.9deg. wood 556px = 1.77x (mask dilation only), bias 0.038. dark bias 0.053. The generator's shadow direction is SHANG=0.9rad = 51.6deg -- the light-background bias angle matches it to 1.3deg. That is the signature: the displacement is ALONG the cast-shadow vector.
raft-marker-placement-open.population: Across 51 count-exact synthetic boards, 43 place well (median 0.059 half-widths, worst 0.136) and 8 get the right number over a wrong picture. SEVEN of those 8 are the -light variant. By background: light p75 0.517 with 6/18 boards over 0.20; dark 0.072 (1/11); noise 0.079 (2/11); wood 0.075 (0/15). A background-dependent defect, NOT a raft-density one -- hexraft, a genuinely fused raft, places at 0.046-0.083 across 14 boards.
raft-marker-placement-open.two-mechanisms: Do not treat all light-background failures as one bug. Coherence (mean bias magnitude / median error) separates them: shadowlone-light reads coherence 1.00, a pure systematic shift = the shadow mechanism above. ttelbow-light reads coherence 0.25 with median 1.306 = large INCOHERENT scatter, a different and still-undiagnosed failure. herringbone-light sits at bias angle 97deg (straight down) not 52deg, so it is also NOT the shadow mechanism despite being -light.
raft-marker-placement-open.gate: tools/raftgate.mjs -- matches markers to EXACT synthetic truth centres and reports median/p90 error in half-widths plus the bias vector and coherence.
raft-marker-placement-open.truth-quality-limit: raftgate can only judge SYNTHETIC boards. The real-photo centres in testdata/centers say in their own method field that they were 'annotated by eye against 100px/50px zoomed coordinate grids' -- ~5px on a ~900px image, which at a 47px pill minor axis is ~0.2 half-widths of granularity before any placement error. Measured: healthy control r-f091e9e9 reads 0.359 through raftgate and 0.022 through centroidgate on the SAME board. The 16x gap is the rulers disagreeing. Never quote a real-photo raftgate number as placement error.
raft-marker-placement-open.superseded-metric: An earlier raft gate inferred seam-straddling from a dark line inside each marker's footprint and reported salmon 44/86 = 51%. DISCARDED, do not rebuild it: no negative control (every healthy board has ZERO raft markers so it was never shown to read clean on a good raft, and it flagged 100% of every board it could measure) and a continuous seam-sample distribution (min 0, med 3, max 7) so the >=3 bar produced the number rather than discovering it. The embossed '150' markings on those pills are a plausible unruled-out confound. The fix was to stop inferring and use the synthetic boards' exact truth instead.
raft-marker-placement-open.next-step: Stop attacking the synthetic shadow mechanism; it does not appear to be what limits real boards. The honest next question is what DOES displace r-2c50d34e, s-eb90778f and s-0bfc44d8, the three worst real boards, all of which have a clean single light and still place worst. Diagnose those three directly rather than assuming the synthetic story transfers. Note also they are the shiny/gloss family, where SAM already runs -- check whether the SAM mask places better than the classical one before building anything new.
raft-marker-placement-open.exact-mechanism: shadowcut is the right stage and runs early enough (line ~2676, long before mask-used at ~8372). It FIRES on adv-shadowpair-light (4556px cut, placement bias 0.058 = good) and NEVER on adv-shadowlone-light (bias 0.676 = bad). Two gates stop it, both measured: (1) BORDER TEST `bgB <= pillB` -- the swallowed shadow component reads bgB=0 pillB=134, it touches ZERO background because the mask has engulfed it entirely, so a test asking whether the dark region is at the blob EDGE cannot see an interior one by construction. (2) SPLIT TEST `vis.size < 0.95*remain` -- with the border test relaxed the component then reads vis=596 of remain=663 = 90%, just under the 95% bar, because cutting a 45%-of-blob interior region leaves ~10% of the remainder disconnected. The shadow lobe is 551px of a 1214px blob.
raft-marker-placement-open.why-deferred: A fix needs BOTH gates relaxed, and both exist to stop shadowcut eating dark PILL material -- scored tablets and embossed markings. The salmon board that started this work has embossed 150 engravings on every pill. Trading a measured placement win on one synthetic board for an unmeasured count regression on real boards with dark markings is the wrong trade at this evidence level. An engulfed-shadow arm was written (bgB===0 AND board arm AND comp >= 0.30*blob) and confirmed to pass gate 1 on 7 of 8 blobs, then reverted at gate 2 rather than relax a second invariant.
raft-marker-placement-open.refuted: The engulfed-shadow arm was BUILT AND TESTED, not merely deferred, and it makes the defect WORSE. Relaxing both gates (border test via bgB===0 + board arm + comp >= 0.30*blob, and the split test for the same components) takes adv-shadowlone-light from 0.676 to 1.458 half-widths -- twice as bad -- with the bias still pointing along the shadow vector at coherence 0.99. It is cutting the WRONG SIDE: removing pill material and leaving the shadow, so the blob centre of mass moves FURTHER into the shadow. The wood control is untouched at 0.032 either way. Do not retry this shape of fix; the problem is not which gate blocks the cut, it is that a component-based cut cannot tell shadow from pill on this board.
raft-marker-placement-open.safety-probe: Separately measured and worth keeping: on real boards the arm would admit NOTHING. salmon (embossed 150 engravings on every pill) 0 interior components, cream-caplets 0, r-f091e9e9 0, s-0bfc44d8 7 interior components but 0 qualifying. So the dark-pill-marking hazard that motivated deferring was not the real blocker -- the fix simply does not work.
raft-marker-placement-open.candidate-b-chromatic-refuted: Chromatic separation was tested and does NOT generalise. On adv-shadowlone-light every population is neutral grey (bright chr 0.338,0.335,0.327; dark 0.348,0.335,0.317) and the bright-vs-dark chromatic distance is 5.1 -- the synthetic board is greyscale, so shadow and pill share a hue BY CONSTRUCTION and there is no chromatic signal to exploit. The wood control separates at 81.9, which is precisely why wood never had the defect. On REAL photos it is board-dependent: salmon on its teal board separates at 75.2, but beige-on-black reads only 12.0. The counter already uses chromaticity in shadowcut dC3/dB3 for this reason, so this is not new leverage.
raft-marker-placement-open.candidate-a-directional-refuted: The directional lead is refuted for REAL photos, and the reason matters. tools/shadowdir.mjs recovers the generator angle to under a degree on synthetics (SHANG 51.6deg read as 51.0/50.8 at consistency 1.000), so the estimator is sound. On the real corpus (37 boards) consistency is BOARD-DEPENDENT, not absent: median 0.609, max 0.964, 11 boards above 0.70 and 4 below 0.40. So a gated directional fix looked possible. It is not: placement error correlates with consistency at Pearson r = +0.332 -- POSITIVE. The three worst-placed real boards (r-2c50d34e 0.181, s-eb90778f 0.153, s-0bfc44d8 0.116) all read consistency 0.87-0.94, while r-76385b11 has effectively NO direction (0.087) and places fine at 0.049. A direction-aimed correction would therefore aim most confidently on exactly the boards whose displacement is not shadow-driven. Correcting along an estimated shadow vector would make the worst boards worse.
raft-marker-placement-open.all-candidates: (a) directional -- refuted above, wrong-signed correlation on real boards. (b) chromatic -- refuted, no signal on greyscale synthetics (bright-vs-dark distance 5.1) and board-dependent on real photos (salmon 75.2, beige-on-black 12.0); the counter already uses it in shadowcut dC3/dB3. (c) component cut -- refuted, relaxing the border and split gates DOUBLES the error (0.676 -> 1.458) by cutting pill material and leaving the shadow.
raft-marker-placement-open.what-is-established: The mechanism is proven on synthetics and the tooling is sound: shadowcut fires on shadowpair-light (bias 0.058) and never on shadowlone-light (bias 0.676), blocked by bgB=0 pillB=134 at the border test then vis 596/663 at the split test. raftgate coherence and shadowdir consistency were built independently and agree on all three light boards, correctly separating three distinct bugs. What is NOT established is that this synthetic mechanism is what drives the real corpus at all -- the positive correlation above is evidence AGAINST it.
raft-marker-placement-open.scale-check: BEFORE SPENDING MORE HERE, note the scale. The corpus now sits at median 0.024 half-widths per board, with 34 of 505 single markers (6.7%) over the 0.25 flag bar and only 4 of 41 boards over 0.10 median. Salmon's remaining 0.130 is 4.9px on a 75px pill = 6.5% of pill width -- well below what reads as "the marker is in the corner". Verified visually: beige-round-black-2 (0.261 -> 0.032) now shows every marker at its pill centre at native resolution, count exact 90/90. The operator-visible defect that started this work is FIXED for stamp singles. What remains is sub-visual on all but four boards, so further placement work should be justified by something other than the metric.

bilateral-crease-denoise-refuted.what: REFUTED lever: replacing the Gaussian pre-blur in cutCreases() with an edge-preserving bilateral filter, on the theory that Gaussian smooths the seam as hard as it smooths the noise and is therefore backwards for a detector whose job is finding that seam.
bilateral-crease-denoise-refuted.evidence: Zero effect. lined-69204ff4 19, lined-503b3041 18, lined-bfdbfef9 19, r-f091e9e9 19 EXACT -- byte-identical to baseline with the patch stashed out. bilateralFilter(5, 40, 40) before the Sobel changes no count and no per-pill figure on any of the four boards tested.
bilateral-crease-denoise-refuted.measurement-error-to-avoid: This lever was motivated by a seam-SNR statistic I computed WRONG and should not be trusted if seen elsewhere. tools/_seamc.mjs (deleted) sampled MASK-INTERIOR pixels at WORKING scale and reported lined-69204ff4 at SNR 4.4 against r-f091e9e9 24 -- a 5.5x deficit that looked like a smoking gun. Measured consistently on full-resolution source luma over all bright pixels, the ordering REVERSES: 69204ff4 reads 15.1 raw / 40.3 gaussian while r-f091e9e9 reads 3.0 / 4.6. The two populations differ in scale, pill size and mask extent, so cross-board comparison of the first statistic is meaningless. Do not conclude anything about noise limiting a board without a scale-normalised, same-population measurement.
bilateral-crease-denoise-refuted.note: The board itself was also mis-read at first: the low-resolution overlay makes the central knot look like caplets OVERLAPPING and stacked (which would be out of scope). The zoom crops show them touching and adjacent at varied angles -- the board is IN scope and the -1 is a genuine failure.

salmon-placement-ground-truth.what: The salmon board now HAS independent centre annotations (testdata/centers/t2-salmon-pentagon-tablets-teal.json, 89 centres, built by tools/annotate-centers.mjs from an HSV colour mask + distance-transform NMS that shares no code path with the counter). This is the first time salmon placement could be measured against anything other than the mask.
salmon-placement-ground-truth.measured: Counter vs annotation on the production decoder: 79 of 89 matched, 10 missed, 13 spurious. Displacement median 16.3px, p90 47.9px, max 62.8px -- on a ~125px pill that worst case is half a pill. Normalised: median 0.261 half-widths, p90 0.769, max 1.008. Coherence 0.11 = scatter, not a shift.
salmon-placement-ground-truth.metrics-that-understated-it: Every mask-relative metric was off by 10-20x on this board: centroidgate on isolated singles 0.130, tools/allmarkers.mjs local-centre-of-mass over ALL 92 markers 0.020 median with ZERO over the 0.25 bar, placegate 0 off-mask, stamp overlap max 0.16. Inside a fused raft the mask is pill material in every direction, so nothing measured against the mask can see this. Only an independent detector could.
salmon-placement-ground-truth.root-cause: All 92 placements are stamp-owned and 52 of 92 sit on an exact 24px lattice at working scale (53 on 12, 55 on 6 -- genuinely 24-multiples). That is js/stamp.js line ~2502: stride = round(0.35 * MIN), which is 24 at this pill size. The seeds are a grid and the refinement cannot move them.
salmon-placement-ground-truth.why-refinement-cannot: MEASURED, and this is the important part. Over the 76 pairs where the annotation and the counter differ by 6..75px, the TRUE centre scores higher on plain coverage only 6 of 76 times (8%). Coverage is not merely saturated on a dense raft -- it actively PREFERS the wrong pose 92% of the time, because a marker straddling two pills covers just as much foreground as one centred on either. A seam-darkness term (interior luma minus boundary-ring luma) scores the truth higher 35 of 76 = 46%, a coin flip. Neither signal can find the true centre. js/stamp.js line ~1510 already records the same wall from the other side: greedy refine cannot escape the coverage plateau, all 7 losers re-refined to their own vetoed pose.
salmon-placement-ground-truth.next-step: Three measurements now agree that no local geometric score fixes this: coverage prefers the wrong pose 92% of the time, seam-darkness is a coin flip at 46%, and the peel objective ties on 79% of pairs. The remaining options are (a) a whole-pill appearance model -- the annotation tool colour+DT approach promoted into the counter, which is a new detector rather than a tweak, or (b) the segmenter, which already runs on this board and takes the count 92 -> 89. Option (b) is shipped; option (a) is a real project. Either way, guard with tools/raftgate.mjs against testdata/centers/t2-salmon-pentagon-tablets-teal.json (current baseline: 79/89 matched, median 0.261 half-widths).
salmon-placement-ground-truth.seeding-is-not-the-blocker: TESTED, and it rules out the obvious fix. The 24px lattice comes from stampArbitrate line ~1173, stride = (min/3)|0, whose grid-indexed gs/gk arrays cannot hold arbitrary seeds -- so DT-peak seeding there means restructuring the peel loop. Before doing that surgery I asked whether PERFECT seeds would even survive: scoring each annotated true centre against the counter marker for the same pill, under the peel loop own objective (elliptical sample set, coverage with a DT-graded background penalty, best of 12 rotations), truth wins 15 of 76 and SIXTY of 76 are EXACT TIES. The objective is flat, so it keeps whatever seed it was given regardless of quality. Better seeds would be discarded by the same score that discards the truth. Do not restructure the peel loop for seeding -- it would not change the outcome.
salmon-placement-ground-truth.also-refuted: Adding DT-peak seeds to sweepWholeImage() had zero effect for a duller reason worth recording: sweepWholeImage has NO CALLER. It is dead code on this path. The live placement is stampArbitrate. Check the call graph before patching a promising-looking function.

dt-snap-stamped-raft.what: FIXED the operator-reported corner markers on stamped rafts. Where the count comes from mass over one fused region, placements were a stride grid (52 of salmon 92 markers on an exact 24px lattice = stampArbitrate stride=(min/3)|0). DT-snap moves each marker to a local maximum of the distance transform over the surface the stamp counted on.
dt-snap-stamped-raft.result: salmon per-pill 79/89 -> 85/89, misses 10 -> 4, spurious 13 -> 7; displacement median 0.261 -> 0.058 half-widths (~16px -> ~3.6px), p90 0.769 -> 0.115. All four gates unchanged (browser 258/262, Node 256/262, adversarial 51/56, per-pill 799/1020); salmon jitter spread 2, unchanged.
dt-snap-stamped-raft.predicate: Fires only when EVERY placement is stamp-owned AND minorSpread == 0 (one template stamped N times) with >= 12 placements. Measured: selects salmon + beige-black-1/-2 + lightblue; silent on r-f091e9e9 (spread 0.356), s-0bfc44d8 (1.14), r-fd69dff9, lined-69204ff4. NOT generic -- outside the regime DT peaks over-detect ~2x with ~0.5 half-width error (r-f091e9e9 59 peaks for 19 pills, s-0bfc44d8 50 for 34).
dt-snap-stamped-raft.bugs-found-on-the-way: (1) PER-MARKER GREEDY ASSIGNMENT SCRAMBLES THE BOARD: an early marker takes a peak belonging to another pill and the error cascades -- that version read 36/89, WORSE than the 79/89 it was fixing. Use global closest-first assignment over all (marker, peak) pairs. (2) DT OVER activeMd IS WRONG: activeMd is a LABELLED watershed map at that point, so the transform measures distance to label boundaries and finds 130 peaks for 92 pills. The standalone probe got 89/89 only because it ran on the mask-used stage. Use stampFgUsed. Same algorithm, wrong input -- check WHICH surface a probe and the live code are each reading before trusting agreement or disagreement.
dt-snap-stamped-raft.peak-count-as-a-counter-REFUTED: The DT peak count is an independent count estimate, and it is NOT reliably better than the arithmetic one. Measured: salmon peaks 91 vs arithmetic 92 (truth 90, so peaks would WIN by 1), beige-black-1 and -2 both 90 vs 90 (tie), but lightblue-1 peaks 75 vs arithmetic 70 (truth 70, so peaks would LOSE by 5). Using peaks to correct counts trades one +1 win for a -5 loss. Placement only.
dt-snap-stamped-raft.remaining: salmon is still 4 misses / 7 spurious against the annotation and 92 for 90 on count. The count is a separate problem from placement and is unchanged by this work.

seam-vertex-veto-refuted.what: REFUTED lever: vetoing salmon phantom markers by CENTRE DARKNESS (footprint median luma minus centre luma). After DT-snap the 3 spurious markers on the Chrome decode visibly sat on the dark Y where three pills meet, and the statistic separated perfectly -- 89 real markers scored -2.9 to 14.5, the 3 phantoms 23.3 / 27.4 / 34.2, an empty band with no overlap. The three other boards in the regime maxed at 5.3 / 6.9 / 2.8, so a bar of 18 looked safe with wide margin.
seam-vertex-veto-refuted.evidence: It worked exactly as designed on the decode it was measured on: salmon 92 -> 89 (from +2 to -1 of truth 90), the other three regime boards untouched and still exact. Then the Node bake read 255/262, down from 256. THE CASUALTY IS THE SAME BOARD: on NODE pixels salmon already counts EXACTLY 90, and the veto took it to 88 by removing two legitimate markers. Measured pre-veto on that decode, salmon max centreDark is 34.1 with the count already correct -- the exact range used as the phantom signature, on markers that are right.
seam-vertex-veto-refuted.lesson: Centre darkness does not identify phantoms. It identifies markers sitting on a dark image feature, which on ONE decode happen to be phantoms and on the other are real pills. The perfect empty band (14.5 to 23.3) was a property of a single decode, not of the mechanism -- and a separation with no overlap is exactly what over-fitting to one sample looks like. ALWAYS check a proposed discriminator on BOTH decodes of the same image before building on it; the dual-pixel gate caught this only after implementation.
seam-vertex-veto-refuted.also-refuted: A seam-RAY test (fraction of radial rays dipping below the local median before one pill radius) was tried first and separated nothing: spurious 0.03-0.39 against matched 0.03-0.44, entirely inside the healthy range.
seam-vertex-veto-refuted.status: Salmon remains 92 for 90 on Chrome pixels and exactly 90 on Node. Placement is fixed (89/89 matched, median 0.058 half-widths); the residual is a COUNT error on one decoder only.
seam-vertex-veto-refuted.reframing: The refutation exposed the real shape of salmon and it is NOT a systematic over-count. Node pixels give exactly 90. Under tools/jitter the seven runs read [90, 92, 90, 91, 91, 90, 91] -- the MODE is 90, which is truth, and three of seven are exact. Chrome simply draws 92, the tail of that distribution. So the remaining salmon error is INSTABILITY (spread 2), not a bias, and any fix that assumes a consistent +2 is fixing a sample rather than a mechanism -- which is precisely how the centre-darkness veto went wrong. Attack the stability, or accept that a mass-derived count on an 85-unit fused region cannot be pinned tighter than +-1 without per-pill evidence.

salmon-instability-traced.what: Traced salmon jitter [90,92,90,91,91,90,91] to its source, and refuted the fix. The count tracks the mega-region unit estimate ONE-FOR-ONE: biggestUnits 83 -> count 90, 84 -> 91, 85 -> 92. Nothing else matters.
salmon-instability-traced.the-chain: The 92 run is the only one whose mask foreground jumps: six runs sit at 88,628-88,950px, run 1 at 91,969 (+3,200). That excess enters at the distance-transform refine, where kept goes 72,250 -> 75,724. The cause is one integer: thr reads 20 on six runs and 19 on the seventh. thr = max(12, min(max(rawOtsu, 0.7*pct), 1.4*pct)); the interpolated percentile anchor pct is stable to a hundredth (19.53-19.55) but rawOtsu is a WHOLE HISTOGRAM BIN and it wins the max(), so its one-bin flip sets the whole difference.
salmon-instability-traced.refuted-fix: Snapping Otsu to the percentile anchor when the two agree within a bin (otsuUse = |rawOtsu-pct| <= 1 ? pct : rawOtsu) DOES stabilise the mask -- foreground spread collapses from 3.6% to 0.1% (92,319-92,426 across all seven runs). But the COUNTS DO NOT CHANGE: still [90,92,90,91,91,90,91], because biggestUnits still varies 83-85 for a different reason. Node bake held at 256/259 with no casualties, and every ratchet image (bfdbfef9, 69204ff4, 0bfc, 503b3041, fd69dff9, 90dbe20e) kept its exact baseline spread. So the change buys no measurable stability anywhere while shifting salmon mask fg by 3.6% -- a real behaviour change with no demonstrated benefit. REVERTED.
salmon-instability-traced.what-this-rules-out: Mask instability is NOT the cause of the count spread. The mask can be made stable and the count still swings, so the variance enters AFTER the mask, in whatever turns mask area into a unit estimate for the 85-unit region. Do not re-attack the threshold.
salmon-instability-traced.next: Instrument the unit-estimate path itself (raft-unit / unitfix / unitprov) across the same seven jitter runs and find what varies while the mask is held fixed. Note the practical ceiling first: jitter mode is already 90 = truth, and 3 of 7 runs are exact, so this is worth at most +1 on one decoder.
salmon-instability-traced.unit-path-traced: TRACED to the end, and there is no arithmetic divisor to stabilise. The mega-region is created by stampArbitrate (js/counter.js ~8357 replaces regions wholesale with verdict.add), and its units EQUALS its placed pill count on every run -- 83 pills = 83 units, 84 = 84, 85 = 85. The stamp PLACES, it does not divide. megaArea is meanwhile stable to 0.22% (436,699-437,663) and singles=16 on all seven runs, so neither area nor the single calibration is the variable. The three area/unit division sites (js/counter.js 4228, 4446, 4530) never fire for this region -- verified by instrumenting each with an area>300000 guard.
salmon-instability-traced.what-the-stamp-is-already-doing: THE HEADLINE, and it changes how the residual should be judged. Pre-stamp counts under the SAME +-1 noise run 72, 81, 90, 95, 98, 120, 129 -- a spread of 57, sd 18.8. Post-stamp they are 90, 92, 90, 91, 91, 90, 91 -- spread 2, sd 0.70. The stamp absorbs 96.3% of the input variance. The remaining spread of 2 is what leaks through an already extreme filter, on a board where the mask+watershed disagree with themselves by nearly a factor of two.
salmon-instability-traced.revised-assessment: Chasing the last +-1 here is not a threshold-tuning problem and not a divisor problem -- it is asking a placement arbiter to be more decode-invariant than the mask it reads. Given jitter mode is already 90 = truth, 3 of 7 runs exact, and placement is now 89/89 matched at 0.058 half-widths, the honest position is that salmon is at its practical ceiling for the classical path. The remaining lever is the segmenter (SAM already takes this board 92 -> 89), not more counter surgery.

lined-69204ff4-placement.what: lined-69204ff4 counts 19 for 20 but matches only 12 of 20 pills on the PRODUCTION decoder, with 7 spurious. Visually the failure is stark: its 15-unit region collapses ALL FIFTEEN markers into one knot at the centre while eight real caplets around it get nothing. Right-ish number, badly wrong picture.
lined-69204ff4-placement.decoder-split: The two decoders segment this board completely differently. Chrome makes ONE 15-unit region (area 13964 = 15.75x medSingle, tagged arc); Node makes two 2-unit regions and a scatter of singles. Same photo. Node matches 17/20, Chrome 12/20, and both report 19.
lined-69204ff4-placement.why-dt-snap-does-not-apply: The salmon fix is correctly scoped out of this board and should stay out. stampedFrac=0.00 and minorSpread=1.13 here, versus 1.00 and 0.000 on the stamped-raft regime. The deeper reason is SHAPE: salmon pills are near-circular (aspect 1.09) so each is one DT point-peak, while these are caplets (aspect 2.07) whose distance transform is a RIDGE running the length of the pill. Peak-finding therefore fragments each caplet -- measured, DT peaks give 18/20 matched but 12-29 SPURIOUS at every suppression radius from 0.4 to 0.7 of the pill width, against salmon 89/89 with ZERO spurious.
lined-69204ff4-placement.also-refuted: DT-CORE CENTROIDS, the natural fix for a ridge: threshold the DT at F*minor, label the connected cores, take each centroid. Spurious drops to 2 (much better than peak-finding) but matching CAPS AT 16/20 with a 12.5px median error on a 24px pill -- half a pill width. Swept F from 0.30 to 0.50: 16/16/13/9/3 matched. The cores merge across caplets that touch end-to-side, so neither peaks nor cores recover individual pills.
lined-69204ff4-placement.assessment: Both centre-finders fail for the same physical reason: these caplets are fused end-to-side at varied angles with no separating gap, so there is no per-pill maximum OR per-pill core to find. stress-suite-findings.ac-isotropy-attempt-REFUTED: The rot90/rot270 inflation on the lined family (+4/+5) and r-2c50d34e was traced to its root and the fix chain was REVERTED after corpus casualties.
